_meta.indication: Treatment of neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) in adult patients who are anti-aquaporin-4 (AQP4) antibody positive.

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.phase: Single adequate and well-controlled efficacy trial (randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter)
pivotal_trials.design: Prospective, double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized trial; patients randomized 3:1 to 300 mg inebilizumab-cdon IV on Day 1 and Day 15 or matching placebo, followed by single 300 mg doses every six months.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with NMOSD; stratified by anti-AQP4 antibody status, with 213 of 230 ITT patients seropositive and 17 seronegative for anti-AQP4 antibodies.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Time, in days, from Day 1 to the first Adjudication Committee (AC)-confirmed relapse (or to Day 197 if no AC-confirmed relapse occurred).
pivotal_trials.n: 230 patients in the ITT population (213 anti-AQP4 seropositive, 17 seronegative); anti-AQP4 positive cohort placebo N=52, inebilizumab N=161.
pivotal_trials.result: In anti-AQP4 antibody positive patients, relapses occurred in 18 (11.2%) of inebilizumab patients vs 22 (42.3%) of placebo; hazard ratio 0.227 (95% CI 0.121, 0.423); p<0.0001 (a 77% relative reduction in adjudicated relapses).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=10% and greater than placebo) were urinary tract infection and arthralgia; across randomized and open-label treatment, the most common (>10%) were urinary tract infection (20%), nasopharyngitis (13%), infusion reaction (12%), arthralgia (11%), and headache (10%). Key risks include infusion reactions, infections (including hepatitis B reactivation and tuberculosis), and reduction in immunoglobulins.
target_moa: Humanized, afucosylated IgG1 kappa monoclonal antibody that binds the CD19 surface antigen on B-cells; binding targets the CD19-expressing cell for depletion via antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC) and antibody-dependent cellular phagocytosis (ADCP).
modality: mAb (humanized afucosylated IgG1 kappa monoclonal antibody)

advisory_committee.vote: Application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the safety profile was acceptable, the trial design acceptable, and efficacy findings clear; no controversial issues warranted committee discussion.

summary.text: Inebilizumab-cdon was developed for NMOSD and granted orphan drug designation (February 10, 2016) and breakthrough therapy designation (March 17, 2019). The BLA, received June 11, 2019, was supported by a single adequate and well-controlled trial (Study 1155) and approved June 11, 2020 without accelerated approval and without advisory committee referral.

citations.quote: This development program was granted orphan drug designation for the treatment of NMOSD on February 10, 2016, and was granted breakthrough therapy designation for the treatment of NMOSD on March 17, 2019 (prior to the approval of Soliris).
The applicant submitted findings from a single adequate and well-controlled efficacy trial in support of this application.

Your application for Uplizna was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the safety profile is acceptable for NMOSD in adult patients who are anti-AQP4 antibody positive, the clinical trial design is acceptable, the efficacy findings are clear, and outside expertise was not necessary; there were no controversial issues that would benefit from advisory committee discussion.

citations.quote: 3869-2 A safety trial to monitor serum immunoglobulin G and M levels in patients with neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) during treatment with UPLIZNA (inebilizumab-cdon) to establish the nadir in circulating immunoglobulins during chronic treatment, and to monitor patients after discontinuation of treatment with UPLIZNA (inebilizumab-cdon) in order to ascertain the time needed to ensure restoration of pre-treatment baseline circulating serum levels of immunoglobulins G and M.
